title: Canonical data and propositions for diagonal section pasting
statement:
Fix the finite coefficient stage $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$, $n\geq1$, of [def-pur-conventions], with the specified global field $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$ and finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $f:X\to Y$ and $g:Y\to Z$ be smooth separated finite-type morphisms of pure relative dimensions $d,e\geq0$ between finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Use the small pro-etale constructible exceptional inverse images and derived operations of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image, def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Put $\omega_h=Rh^!\Lambda$ and let $c_{v,u}:R(vu)^!\xrightarrow{\sim}Ru^!Rv^!$ be the conjugate of compact-support composition [thm-sf-comp-composition, def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction, def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate]. Let $\theta_{h,M}:Lh^*M\otimes^L\omega_h\to Rh^!M$ be the specified tensor map [def-pur-co-smoothness]. For composable smooth maps $u,v$ define
$$\sigma_{u,v}=c_{v,u,\Lambda}^{-1}\circ\theta_{u,\omega_v}\circ\mathrm{sym}:\omega_u\otimes^LLu^*\omega_v\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{vu}.$$
For $h=f,g,gf$, write $W_h=\operatorname{dom}(h)\times_{\operatorname{cod}(h)}\operatorname{dom}(h)$, $p_h$ for its first projection, $\Delta_h$ for the diagonal, $C_h=L\Delta_h^*\omega_{p_h}$ [def-pur-section-invariant], and $\alpha_h:C_h\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_h$ for the specified diagonal base-change map [lem-pur-diagonal-base-change].

Put $Q=X\times_ZY$, $W=X\times_ZX$, $a:W\to Q$, $(x_1,x_2)\mapsto(x_1,f(x_2))$, $b:Q\to X$, $(x,y)\mapsto x$, $t=\Delta_{gf}:X\to W$, and $s=(\operatorname{id}_X,f):X\to Q$. These formulas denote the maps induced by the fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product]. Then $at=s$, $ba=p_{gf}$, and the Cartesian base-change maps identify $C_f\cong Lt^*\omega_a$ and $Lf^*C_g\cong Ls^*\omega_b$. Define the section-pasting comparison, using these maps and the monoidal pullback reassociation, by
$$\kappa:C_f\otimes^LLf^*C_g\xrightarrow{\sim}Lt^*(\omega_a\otimes^LLa^*\omega_b)\xrightarrow{Lt^*\sigma_{a,b}}C_{gf}.$$
Define Equation to be the proposition
$$\alpha_{gf}\circ\kappa=\sigma_{f,g}\circ(\alpha_f\otimes Lf^*\alpha_g).$$
For compatible source and target open immersions, define the restriction comparison for a smooth dualizing object by first making the target-open Cartesian base change, then applying the counit-normalized etale exceptional restriction for the residual source-open immersion [lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality]. Restriction of a section object uses the corresponding map on both factors of its self-product and the pullback-composition isomorphism. These give restriction comparisons for every source and target below. Define OpenEquation as the conjunction of naturality squares for alpha_f, alpha_g, alpha_(gf), sigma_(f,g), kappa, and the two input comparisons gamma_f:C_f to t^*omega_a and gamma_g:f^*C_g to s^*omega_b. In each square, pull back the old arrow and follow the codomain restriction comparison, and equate this with the domain restriction comparison followed by the new arrow. Tensor sources use the canonical monoidal pullback comparison, with the pullback compositor on their second factor. The two gamma codomains use the maps on W and Q induced by the same open immersions. This defines seven specific equality propositions; none is asserted here.

For the coordinate comparison, use the following additional constructions. For a separated finite-type $k$-scheme $B$, put $P_r=\mathbf A^r_B\to B$ [def-sbc-affine-space], let $z_r:B\to\mathbf A^r_B$ be its zero section, and put $D_r=Lz_r^*\omega_{P_r}$. Let $q:\mathbf A^{d+e}_B=\mathbf A^d_{\mathbf A^e_B}\to\mathbf A^e_B$. Base change for the square defining $q$ identifies $Lz_{d+e}^*\omega_q$ with $D_d$, while pullback composition identifies $Lz_{d+e}^*Lq^*\omega_{P_e}$ with $D_e$. Define
$$\nu_{d,e}:D_d\otimes^LD_e\xrightarrow{\sim}Lz_{d+e}^*(\omega_q\otimes^LLq^*\omega_{P_e})\xrightarrow{Lz_{d+e}^*\sigma_{q,P_e}}D_{d+e}.$$
On compatible etale [def-weil-etale-morphism] coordinate charts $U\to\mathbf A^d_V$, $V\to\mathbf A^e_T$ for $f,g$, with $U,V,T$ affine open subschemes of $X,Y,Z$, the coordinate differences in the second factors of the diagonal pairs identify $C_f|_U$, $Lf^*C_g|_U$, $C_{gf}|_U$ with $D_d,D_e,D_{d+e}$ over $B=U$. Define ChartEquation to be the proposition $\kappa|_U=\nu_{d,e}$ under these comparisons, for a given affine chart triple. These are the canonical etale exceptional-pullback comparisons and monoidal pullback comparisons, and use no diagonal orientation or Tate-twist identification.

Define ModelStatement to be Equation together with, for every compatible open restriction, OpenEquation and, for every pair of compatible etale affine-space charts on that restriction, ChartEquation. The repeated Noetherian, finiteness and smoothness instances are supplied by the given finite-type structure maps and compatible open squares. Define Statement by specializing ModelStatement to the prescribed finite coefficient quotient, with its canonical invertible exponent. This node constructs the maps and defines these propositions; it does not assert Equation, OpenEquation, ChartEquation or Statement. All data are explicit composites of the specified canonical maps, with no orientation or arbitrary witness choice.

source.place: Step 1, canonical diagonal section, open restriction and ordered affine-coordinate constructions

proof.text: Lean helper proofs (J8, partial completion): obtain the coefficient exponent from the finite comparison theorem. The canonical tensor map is invertible by cohomological smoothness; the canonical dualizing base-change map is invertible by smooth exceptional base change, using affine locality to avoid an extra quasi-separatedness hypothesis. Construct both squares of geometry by the pullback universal property and check their section identities by projections. Base change gives the relative dimension and separated finite-type properties of a; composition gives dimension d+e. Finite-type quasi-compact projections over Noetherian schemes give noetherianPullback and affineNoetherian. For affineGeometry, split a (d+e)-tuple into its first d and last e coordinates; concatenate the two tuples for the inverse universal map, and check equality on the base and each coordinate. The zero tuples give the section identities, and q is the base change of the d-space projection. The remaining open-factor, open-pair and open-middle claims follow from projection identities, stability of open immersions under base change and composition cancellation. These are proved in Lean. Y2 completes chartGeometry: base change each etale affine-space chart and compose with translation by the negative first-factor coordinates. Translation by the opposite vector is its inverse. For the total chart use affine d-space over Q as the explicit intermediate scheme; its block-insertion map J is the Cartesian base change of the second difference chart, and its translated first-chart map H is etale. Equality on the base and every ordered coordinate proves H followed by J is the total difference map. Affine sources and targets supply separatedness and quasi-compactness; etaleness supplies local finite type. Evaluating the difference coordinates on the diagonal or graph section gives zero. Empty blocks are handled by Fin.addCases without nonemptiness assumptions. E9 preserves these proofs in the shared data module and calls Scheme.pullback_map_isOpenImmersion directly for the first conjuncts of openPairProperties and openMiddleProperties, avoiding slow broad instance search without changing their statements.

Construct sigma from the specified smooth theta isomorphism and inverse exceptional compositor, alpha from inverse self-product beta followed by the diagonal section compositor, and gamma_f and gamma_g from the two Cartesian restrictions. Define kappa and nu by tensoring these canonical input comparisons, using the monoidal pullback comparison and applying pullback to sigma. Construct each open comparison by target-open base change and counit-normalized source-etale restriction. Define Equation, OpenEquation and ChartEquation as the displayed equality propositions, then form their quantified conjunction ModelStatement and specialize to the finite coefficient quotient to obtain Statement. These are explicit definitions, not existence choices or assertions of the unproved equality propositions.

    (d e : ℕ) (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    [IsSeparated f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f]
    [IsSeparated g] [LocallyOfFiniteType g] [QuasiCompact g]
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension d f] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension e g]
